body:
### Problem

Example of `.` mapping in `:h edit-repeat` doesn't work well with `nvim_feedkeys(..., 'mt', false)` while the built-in dot-repeat works. Note: there is a `t` flag which is expected to be covered by the `CmdAtom` approach based on [this comment](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/41387#issuecomment-5372357174).

This was observed in practical usage with plugin(s) that provide custom mapping execution that shows clues about them while they are typed (in my case - 'mini.clue').

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create `init.lua` with the following content:

    ```lua
    _G.log = {}

    -- Implement `:h edit-repeat` with tracking of all `CmdAtom` events
    local last ---@type vim.event.cmdatom.data?
    local maxseq = {} ---@type table<integer, integer>
    vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd('CmdAtom', {
      callback = function(ev)
        table.insert(_G.log, { data = ev.data, maxseq_buf = maxseq[ev.buf] })

        local is_redo_or_undo = ev.data.changed and (ev.data.undoseq or 0) <= (maxseq[ev.buf] or 0)
        maxseq[ev.buf] = vim.fn.undotree(ev.buf).seq_last
        if ev.data.changed and not is_redo_or_undo and ev.data.lhs ~= '.' then last = ev.data end
      end,
    })
    vim.keymap.set('n', '.', function()
      -- CmdAtom is deferred; schedule the replay, in case "." follows an edit.
      vim.schedule(function()
        if last then vim.api.nvim_feedkeys(last.keys or last.lhs, last.keys and 'n' or 'm', false) end
      end)
    end)

    -- Custom mapping that uses `nvim_feedkeys(..., 'mt', false)`
    vim.keymap.set('n', '<M-m>', function() vim.api.nvim_feedkeys('dl', 'mt', false) end)

    -- Prepare buffer text for repro
    vim.api.nvim_buf_set_lines(0, 0, -1, false, { 'aaa' })
    vim.bo.modified = false
    ```

2. `nvim --clean -u init.lua`.

3. There are two examples that have problems. In both cases the built-in dot-repeat works.

    3.1. Press `<M-m>`. It deletes a character under cursor as expected.

    3.2. `:lua vim.api.nvim_feedkeys('dl', 'mt', false)`. It deletes a character under cursor as expected.

4. Press `.`. Nothing happens.

The reason this happens is because `is_redo_or_undo` check is `true` during execution of `nvim_feedkeys` because there was a previous `CmdAtom` event that updated the `maxseq`.

Here are the output of `:=_G.log`:

<details><summary>Log for 3.1.</summary>

```lua
{ {
  data = {
    changed = false,
    lhs = "<80><fc>\bm",
    moved = false,
    pos = { 1, 0 },
    type = "mapping",
    undoseq = 1
  },
  is_redo_or_undo = false
}, {
  data = {
    changed = true,
    cmd = "l",
    keys = "dl",
    lhs = "dl",
    moved = false,
    operator = "d",
    pos = { 1, 0 },
    type = "operator",
    undoseq = 2
  },
  is_redo_or_undo = true,
  maxseq_buf = 2
}, {
  data = {
    changed = false,
    lhs = ".",
    moved = false,
    pos = { 1, 0 },
    type = "mapping",
    undoseq = 2
  },
  is_redo_or_undo = false,
  maxseq_buf = 2
} }
```

</details>

<details><summary>Log for 3.2.</summary>

```lua
{ {
  data = {
    changed = false,
    cmd = ":",
    keys = ":lua vim.api.nvim_feedkeys('dl', 'mt', false)\n",
    lhs = ":lua vim.api.nvim_feedkeys('dl', 'mt', false)\n",
    moved = false,
    pos = { 1, 0 },
    text = "lua vim.api.nvim_feedkeys('dl', 'mt', false)",
    type = "excmd",
    undoseq = 1
  },
  is_redo_or_undo = false
}, {
  data = {
    changed = true,
    cmd = "l",
    keys = "dl",
    lhs = "dl",
    moved = false,
    operator = "d",
    pos = { 1, 0 },
    type = "operator",
    undoseq = 2
  },
  is_redo_or_undo = true,
  maxseq_buf = 2
}, {
  data = {
    changed = false,
    lhs = ".",
    moved = false,
    pos = { 1, 0 },
    type = "mapping",
    undoseq = 2
  },
  is_redo_or_undo = false,
  maxseq_buf = 2
} }
```

</details>

### Expected behavior

Documented approach of enhanced `.` that repeats the last edit works in all cases of text edit where the built-in `.` works.

### Nvim version (nvim -v)

NVIM v0.13.0-dev-1410+g510f61555b

### Vim (not Nvim) behaves the same?

No, doesn't have this functionality

### Operating system/version

EndeavourOS Linux x86_64, 7.1.9-arch1-2

### Terminal name/version

Ghostty 1.3.1-arch2

### $TERM environment variable

xterm-ghostty

### Installation

Appimage

comment_data.body:
Although it is recommended to use `t` flag in the `nvim_feedkeys()` when dealing with `CmdAtom`, I'd also point out that `nvim_feedkeys(..., 'm', false)` works with built-in dot-repeat.

In particular, what caught my attention is that `CmdAtom` event has `data.changed=false`. With this issue's `init.lua`, the output of `_G.log` after `` is like this:

<details><summary>Log for 3.2.</summary>

```lua
{ {
  data = {
    changed = false,
    cmd = ":",
    keys = ":lua vim.api.nvim_feedkeys('dl', 'm', false)\n",
    lhs = ":lua vim.api.nvim_feedkeys('dl', 'm', false)\n",
    moved = false,
    pos = { 1, 0 },
    text = "lua vim.api.nvim_feedkeys('dl', 'm', false)",
    type = "excmd",
    undoseq = 1
  },
  is_redo_or_undo = false
}, {
  data = {
    changed = false,
    lhs = ".",
    moved = false,
    pos = { 1, 0 },
    type = "mapping",
    undoseq = 2
  },
  is_redo_or_undo = false,
  maxseq_buf = 2
} }
```

</details>

I.e. this doesn't work with the `CmdAtom` based `.` (**although** it doesn't have the `is_redo_or_undo = true` issue), but works with built-in dot-repeat.

title: CmdAtom: example in `:h edit-repeat` doesn't work with `nvim_feedkeys(..., 'mt', false)`
